# google_memorystore_auth_token

Represents an Auth Token for a Token Auth User within a Google Cloud Memorystore instance.

When token-based authentication (`TOKEN_AUTH`) is enabled on an instance (for the `default` user) or when a token auth user is created, an initial token (`version-1`) is automatically created by the API. Setting `token_id` on create (for example, `token_id = "version-1"`) acquires and manages that existing token in Terraform state instead of creating a new one, returning an error if no token with that ID exists. Omitting `token_id` creates a new server-assigned token version (`version-N`).

Each user can have at most 2 active tokens at a time and must retain at least 1 active token. To perform zero-downtime token rotation, declare two `google_memorystore_auth_token` resources (acquiring `version-1` with `token_id = "version-1"` on the first resource and creating `version-2` by omitting `token_id` on the second), update client applications to use the new token, and then remove the old token resource from the Terraform configuration.


To get more information about AuthToken, see:

* [API documentation](https://cloud.google.com/memorystore/docs/valkey/reference/rest/v1/projects.locations.instances.tokenAuthUsers.authTokens)
* How-to Guides
    * [Official Documentation](https://cloud.google.com/memorystore/docs/valkey/)

~> **Note:** Deleting the sole remaining token for a user is rejected by the API. Set `deletion_policy = "ABANDON"` to remove a user's last remaining token from Terraform state without calling the delete API (for example, before destroying the parent user or instance).

~> **Warning:** All arguments including the following potentially sensitive
values will be stored in the raw state as plain text: `token`.
[Read more about sensitive data in state](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/manage-sensitive-data).

## Example Usage - Memorystore Auth Token Basic


```hcl
resource "google_memorystore_instance" "token-basic-instance" {
  instance_id                 = "token-basic-instance"
  shard_count                 = 1
  node_type                   = "SHARED_CORE_NANO"
  location                    = "europe-west4"
  authorization_mode          = "TOKEN_AUTH"
  deletion_protection_enabled = false
}

resource "google_memorystore_auth_token" "token-basic" {
  instance                    = google_memorystore_instance.token-basic-instance.instance_id
  user_id                     = "default"
  location                    = "europe-west4"
}
```

## Example Usage - Memorystore Auth Token Rotation


```hcl
resource "google_memorystore_instance" "instance" {
  instance_id                 = "token-rotation-instance"
  shard_count                 = 1
  node_type                   = "SHARED_CORE_NANO"
  location                    = "europe-west4"
  authorization_mode          = "TOKEN_AUTH"
  deletion_protection_enabled = false
}

resource "google_memorystore_auth_token" "token-1" {
  instance = google_memorystore_instance.instance.instance_id
  user_id  = "default"
  token_id = "version-1"
  location = "europe-west4"
}

resource "google_memorystore_auth_token" "token-2" {
  instance   = google_memorystore_instance.instance.instance_id
  user_id    = "default"
  location   = "europe-west4"
  depends_on = [google_memorystore_auth_token.token-1]
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are supported:


* `location` -
  (Required)
  The location of the Memorystore instance.

* `instance` -
  (Required)
  The ID or resource name of the Memorystore instance.

* `user_id` -
  (Required)
  The unique ID (username) of the Token Auth User.


* `token_id` -
  (Optional)
  The ID of the auth token (for example, `version-1`), or its full resource name.
  If specified, Terraform acquires and manages the existing active token with this ID (such as the initial `version-1` token automatically created with the instance or user) and returns an error if it does not exist.
  If omitted, a new token version will be created on the server.

* `project` - (Optional) The ID of the project in which the resource belongs.
    If it is not provided, the provider project is used.

* `deletion_policy` - (Optional) Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the resource. Defaults to DELETE.
	When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the resource,
	the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
	When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
	management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
	When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.


## Attributes Reference

In addition to the arguments listed above, the following computed attributes are exported:

* `id` - an identifier for the resource with format `projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/instances/{{instance}}/tokenAuthUsers/{{user_id}}/authTokens/{{token_id}}`

* `name` -
  The full resource name of the Auth Token.

* `token` -
  The generated auth token string.
  **Note**: This property is sensitive and will not be displayed in the plan.

* `create_time` -
  The creation time of the auth token.

* `state` -
  The current state of the Auth Token.
  Possible values:
  ACTIVE
  CREATING
  DELETING

This resource provides the following

- `create` - Default is 20 minutes.
- `delete` - Default is 20 minutes.

## Import


AuthToken can be imported using any of these accepted formats:

* `projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/instances/{{instance}}/tokenAuthUsers/{{user_id}}/authTokens/{{token_id}}`
* `{{project}}/{{location}}/{{instance}}/{{user_id}}/{{token_id}}`
* `{{location}}/{{instance}}/{{user_id}}/{{token_id}}`

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, use an [`identity` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/block/import#identity) to import AuthToken using identity values. For example:

```tf
import {
  identity = {
    tokenId = "<-optional value->"
    location = "<-required value->"
    instance = "<-required value->"
    userId = "<-required value->"
    project = "<-optional value->"
  }
  to = google_memorystore_auth_token.default
}
```

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import AuthToken using one of the formats above. For example:

```tf
import {
  id = "projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/instances/{{instance}}/tokenAuthUsers/{{user_id}}/authTokens/{{token_id}}"
  to = google_memorystore_auth_token.default
}
```

When using the [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import), AuthToken can be imported using one of the formats above. For example:

```
$ terraform import google_memorystore_auth_token.default projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/instances/{{instance}}/tokenAuthUsers/{{user_id}}/authTokens/{{token_id}}
$ terraform import google_memorystore_auth_token.default {{project}}/{{location}}/{{instance}}/{{user_id}}/{{token_id}}
$ terraform import google_memorystore_auth_token.default {{location}}/{{instance}}/{{user_id}}/{{token_id}}
```
